tables.reason: One row per SKU with currency, net price, tax rate, price list, and validity date; this is a commercial price list rather than a product master or stock table.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Unique 12-value SKU column; leading zeros must be preserved, matching the commercial-offer identity key.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Human-readable product name, one distinct value per SKU, suitable as the offer description.

columns.name: Currency
columns.reason: Contains explicit ISO currency codes SGD and USD; values must be passed through without FX conversion.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Unit of sale (PCS), but the commercial-offer contract has no sales-unit pointer.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Explicit price-list designation, constant 'standard'; no target pointer exists in the commercial-offer contract.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Numeric supplied price, complete for every row; operator instruction says to map net price without tax adjustment.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Explicit 'No' for all rows, indicating the net price is tax-exclusive; the contract only requires the tax fraction, not an inclusion flag.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Explicit 5% source value for every row; convert the percentage to the fractional value 0.05 required by the contract.

columns.name: Valid from (DD/MM/YYYY)
columns.reason: Header explicitly states DD/MM/YYYY, and the constant value 03/04/2026 therefore means 2026-03-04.

changes_from_draft: Completed the field set: added /description (Product name), /money/net_amount (Net price) and /money/tax_fraction (Tax rate → fraction), which the draft left unmatched.
/item_code now casts the trimmed SKU to string without stripping leading zeros (operator requirement); draft used a generic whitespace normalise with low confidence 0.4.
/money/iso_currency: trimmed and upper-cased before an explicit SGD/USD map with keep_unmapped=true; values come from the file, no FX conversion.
/valid_from: the header itself states DD/MM/YYYY, so parse_date_th is pinned to day-first with format %d/%m/%Y; the draft open question about date order is resolved by source evidence and withdrawn.
Dropped the draft question about SKU identity: SKU is unique (12/12), so it is the offer identity — no business decision needed.
Set attributes_passthrough=false and provenance=false: the commercial-offer schema sets additionalProperties=false and has no /attributes, so passthrough would violate the contract.

'Sales unit' (PCS), 'Price list' (standard) and 'Tax included' (No) have no pointer in this contract and cannot be passed through; 'standard' is not hard-coded as a constant anywhere since the contract cannot carry it.
Record dedupe keys set to /item_code (identity key) and quality rules added for required fields, uniqueness, positive price and tax fraction range.
No VAT adjustment applied to Net price: operator requirement says map supplied net price as-is.
